title: How IoT devices are classified: type, category, classification

prose.label: Names need a lookup.
prose.text: {{taxonomy-served-by-endpoints}} The endpoints and record fields are in [[zia.iot.api-surface]].

prose.label: Unknown and the evaluation window.
prose.text: {{unknown-means-limited-information}} {{evaluation-window}} How long a device stays in view and when a location starts producing data is in [[zia.iot.discovery]].
The inputs, thresholds and confidence of the engine are open {{gap:classification-inputs}}; see the input-signals gap in [[zia.iot.discovery]].

checks.do: Whether stored UUIDs are still current, since whether they are stable across model updates is open.

three-level-parentage.statement: Classification is a three-level hierarchy: a device category's parent is a device type, and a device classification's parent is a device category.

quotes: The parent of device category is device type.
The parent of device classification is device category.

device-carries-all-levels.statement: Each discovered device record carries a device-type UUID, a category UUID and a classification UUID, plus `autoLabel`, a label the AI/ML engine generates to describe the device's prominent characteristics.

quotes: A label generated by the Zscaler AI/ML engine to describe the device's prominent characteristics.

unknown-means-limited-information.statement: A device the engine cannot classify lands in the Unknown device type, which the help page defines as devices not classified due to limited information for the AI/ML engine.

quotes: Unknown (Devices not classified due to limited information for the AI/ML engine)

evaluation-window.statement: Each device record has `flowStartTime` and `flowEndTime`, in epoch seconds, marking when the engine started and stopped evaluating the device's weblog records.

quotes: The start timestamp at which Zscaler AI/ML engine starts evaluating the device's weblog records. It's noted in epoch seconds.
The end timestamp at which Zscaler AI/ML engine stops evaluating the device's weblog records. It's noted in epoch seconds.

taxonomy-served-by-endpoints.statement: The UUID-to-name mappings for device types, categories and classifications are served by three separate read-only GET endpoints; a device record holds only UUIDs, so names need a lookup against those lists.
taxonomy-served-by-endpoints.conditions: Chain of evidence: the deviceList schema has UUID fields and no name fields, while the three taxonomy endpoints return uuid, name and parent_uuid.

uuid-stability.title: Whether taxonomy UUIDs are stable across Zscaler model updates
uuid-stability.blocks: storing UUIDs in automation or filters
uuid-stability.detail: Unverified legacy statement: that the taxonomy is returned dynamically, it is unclear whether UUIDs are stable across ML model updates, and stored UUIDs could silently go stale. No source states the stability of the identifiers. Safe handling until resolved: look names up on each run rather than storing UUIDs.

classification-inputs.title: What evidence the engine needs to assign a classification
classification-inputs.detail: No registered source states the inputs, thresholds or confidence of the AI/ML engine; see the input-signals gap in zia.iot.discovery.
